judge: claude-opus-5-5 (medium, fresh independent subagent per group per round; saw neither the author's opinion nor earlier verdicts)

criteria.text:
# jp_city new-pixel adversarial VQA — fixed criteria (do not change between rounds)

You are an adversarial visual QA judge for 16px pixel art in the `jp_city` chipset of a top-down JRPG drawn in **3/4 view**
(camera south of the subject, looking down about 45 degrees). Your job is to find real defects. Do not be polite.
You have not seen any earlier verdicts and you get nobody's opinion about these pictures.

Each candidate board shows every candidate at **1x** (true game size) and **4x**. Each `ref-*.png` board shows
**original jp_city pieces of the same kind** (already in the shipped chipset) at 1x and 4x. The originals are the quality bar.
Judge every candidate against those originals, at both 1x and 4x. Use the Read tool to open every image you are given.

A candidate FAILS if any of these is clearly true:

1. **View (3/4).** A standing object (building, vehicle, tree trunk/crown base, prop) must show its top surfaces seen from above
   (roof planes, flat roofs with a visible top plane, car roof/hood/trunk tops, foreshortened) **and** its south front face.
   Pure side or front elevation with no visible top plane, or pure plan view with almost no front face, fails.
   Vehicles facing east/west show their side profile as the south face plus the roof/hood tops above it. Ground tiles must read as
   flat ground seen from above.
2. **Shading craft vs the originals.** Main materials have clearly fewer value steps than the same material in the originals,
   or large single-colour areas (about 5x5 px or more) with no texture where the originals carry texture, or muddy/blurred/
   noise-like clusters where the originals have clean readable pixel clusters.
3. **Outline.** Outlines are neutral black/grey wrapped around everything where the originals use dark tones of the adjacent material.
4. **Palette/coherence.** Colours or contrast clash with the originals so that the piece would look foreign next to them in one map.
5. **Tiling (ground cells and scenes only).** Visible tile-grid artefacts in a composed map: square/rectangular blocks snapped to the
   16px grid, hard straight seams, obviously repeated stamps, or a hard ruler-straight boundary between the new ground and the
   neighbouring original ground that the originals do not have. Ground autotile cells are variants: judge the cell sheet for pixel
   quality and the **scenes** for how they actually look when laid.
6. **Readability at 1x.** At game size it does not read as what it is named.

Relative rule (fixed): a trait that the originals share to the same degree is not a defect of the candidate.
Tree sprites are never seen alone in game; they overlap in forests — use the forest scenes for crown/trunk/ground judgement as well.

Output: JSON only, written to the file you are told, schema:
```
{"schema":"jp-vqa/1","judge":"claude-opus-5-5","group":"<group>","overall":"PASS|FAIL",
 "items":[{"label":"<label exactly as printed on the board>","verdict":"PASS|FAIL","criteria":[<numbers violated>],
           "reasons":"<concrete: where (rows/area), what, compared with which original>","fix":"<what to change if FAIL>"}]}
```
`overall` is PASS only if every item is PASS. Every label on your boards must appear exactly once.

Greens sit within the zelkova original's hue range.

items.label: jp_city/jp-rg-bamboo-grove
items.reasons: Leaf canopy (top ~40% of the sprite) is a speckled mid/dark-green dither with no readable leaf clusters and no clear light side; compare jp-rg-pine and zelkova originals, whose foliage is clean masses with a lit band and a shade band plus a few highlight dashes. The canopy reads as a lumpy broccoli/cloud cap sitting on the culms rather than drooping sasa leaf fans; the culm area below (dark interior between stalks) is good. A stray brown stub sticks out under the base at centre.
items.fix: Redraw the canopy as distinct drooping leaf fans/sprays (pointed leaf clusters hanging down off the culm tops) with 3-4 clean value steps, lit on the upper-left, instead of dithered noise; let culm tops poke into the canopy; remove or integrate the stray brown stub at the base.

items.label: jp_city/jp-rg-bamboo-grove-b
items.reasons: Same noise-dithered canopy as the grove: no clean cluster structure or light direction, and the upper-left crown lump is a flat-topped boxy block with a straight right edge. Canopy reads as a generic tree crown rather than bamboo leaves; quality below the pine/zelkova originals' clean foliage masses.
items.fix: Rebuild canopy as tapering, drooping bamboo leaf sprays with clean lit/shade clusters; break up the boxy top lump into irregular pointed fans.

items.label: jp_city/jp-rg-bamboo-clump
items.reasons: At 4x the canopy is a muddy blob of mixed greens with a grey hole in the middle-top and no leaf form; at 1x it reads as a small green bush on sticks rather than bamboo. Base: a dark-green rectangular block sticks out to the right beyond the outlined footprint and a brown stub sits at bottom-right, which looks like an artefact.
items.fix: Fewer, clearer culms with nodes reaching higher, topped by distinct drooping leaf sprays with clean value steps; fix the base footprint (remove the protruding dark rectangle and stray stub, give a small soft ground patch like the pine's).

items.label: floor-cells
items.reasons: Lawn-based cells (rows 1-3) keep the original lawn 3281-3283 dot texture across both lit and shaded parts, so no flat 5x5 areas; the shade is two-to-three values deeper and stays in the same hue family. Moss-based cells (rows 3-5) match the shipped moss-and-leaf floor seen in the shrine scene in hue, speckle density and pink/green leaf flecks; at 1x they read as forest floor. In isolation (floor-1x sheet) the shade wedges have stepped 45-degree hypotenuses that look a little geometric, but laid in ex/grove/thin/road scenes they merge into soft, irregular shadow pools under the crowns with no 16px blocks, no ruler-straight seams and no visible repeated stamp. Edges against the original lawn are not detectable at 1x or 4x; in the shrine scene the floor meets the original gravel and stone wall only at those tiles' own drawn edges.

items.label: apron-cells
items.reasons: The shade overlay on lawn and moss keeps the underlying texture (dots/speckles still visible through the shade), without the flat dark fills, black outlines or palette shift that would look foreign next to originals. In scenes (grove-4x, road-4x, thin-4x) the apron reads as a soft southeast cast shadow at the forest edge that fades into the plain lawn; no grid-aligned rectangles, straight cut-offs or obvious repeats, including next to the original road strip in road-4x and around the park lawn tree in street-4x. Minor: in the 1x apron sheet a few cells have rather regular diagonal stair-step boundaries, but they never show once laid.
